To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the information structure of the model is crucial in determining the Fisher information for the parameters of discrete response models, and (b) in incomplete information models, the Fisher information for interaction terms can be positive even when the payoff shock is independent of the observable covariate, and hence, the econometrician has more information about interaction terms than the economic agents.

(1) in the complete information case there is zero Fisher Information for interaction parameters, (2) in the incomplete information case there is positive Fisher Information for interaction paramaters, and (3) in the case of unobserved heteogeneity, the Fisher Information in the incomplete information setting can be larger or smaller than that in the complete setting depending on the tail behavior of the distribution of unobservables.

the information structure in discrete response models matters for statistical information, which has implications for estimation and inference, and that the Fisher information in incomplete information models is non-trivial and can be bounded.
